casefile.title: The Last Toast at Rosewood Manor
casefile.location: Rosewood Manor, the study on the first floor
casefile.summary: During his anniversary dinner, Edmund Rosewood excused himself to his study for a quiet toast. Minutes later a scream rang through the manor. Edmund was found slumped over his desk beside a half-empty brandy glass. The study window was latched from the inside, and the only door opens onto a hallway. Four people had reasons to be at the manor tonight, and one of them is lying.

suspect.name: Clara Rosewood
suspect.statement: I was in the attic studio painting from about half past eight. I heard the scream and ran down the stairs. I loved my uncle, even if he had just cut my allowance.
suspect.alibi: Says she was alone in the attic studio from 8:30 PM until the scream. Nobody saw her there.
suspect.motive: Edmund had cut her allowance and threatened to stop paying her tuition.

suspect.name: Victor Hale
suspect.statement: We argued about the sale of the Rosewood collection. I left at 8:45 sharp, drove home and did not come back. I only learned about the death when the police phoned me.
suspect.alibi: Claims he left the manor before 9 PM and was at home when the police called.
suspect.motive: Edmund suspected Victor of undervaluing items to pocket the difference.

suspect.name: Mrs. Agnes Pritchard
suspect.statement: I poured Mr. Rosewood his brandy from a fresh bottle at 8:58 and left the tray in the hallway outside his study, as I always do. After that I was in the kitchen with the cook all night.
suspect.alibi: The cook says Mrs. Pritchard was in the kitchen from 9:00 PM onward.
suspect.motive: Edmund had told her he planned to sell the manor, ending thirty years of service.

suspect.name: Dr. Julian Marsh
suspect.statement: I was at my clinic until 9:30, then drove over because Edmund asked me to join the toast. I arrived at 9:35, just as the scream rang out, and I pronounced him dead.
suspect.alibi: Says he was working late at his clinic until 9:30 PM and reached the manor at 9:35 PM.
suspect.motive: Edmund had recently asked him odd questions about patient records and prescriptions.

evidence.title: Crime scene report
evidence.description: Edmund Rosewood was found slumped over his desk at 9:40 PM. A half-empty brandy glass sat beside him. The study window was latched from the inside, and the door opens onto the main hallway.

evidence.title: Toxicology note
evidence.description: Cause of death was an overdose of digitoxin, a heart medication, dissolved in the brandy. The dose was large and fast acting. Whoever did this had access to the drug and knew how to dose it.

evidence.title: Front gate camera log
evidence.description: 8:52 PM: the silver sedan of Victor Hale leaves the estate. 8:55 PM: a dark green car registered to Dr. Julian Marsh enters. No other vehicles are logged before the police arrive.
evidence.found_at: Security booth at the front gate

evidence.title: Kitchen record
evidence.description: The cook confirms Mrs. Pritchard poured the brandy at 8:58 PM from a freshly sealed bottle in front of her, then stayed in the kitchen. The tray was left unattended in the hallway for about twenty minutes until Edmund collected it at 9:20 PM.

evidence.title: Livestream recording of Clara
evidence.description: Clara streamed herself painting in the attic studio from 8:30 PM to 9:45 PM. The video is continuous and timestamped, and her easel is visible the whole time.

evidence.title: Pharmacy records
evidence.description: Digitoxin was dispensed three weeks ago on a prescription signed by Dr. Julian Marsh, for a patient who had died two months earlier.

evidence.title: Final diary entry
evidence.description: Found the pharmacy slips for Mrs. Dalton, who died in August. J. signed every one. Told him he has until Monday to explain, or I go to the medical board.

solution.explanation: Dr. Julian Marsh poisoned the brandy with digitoxin, a heart medication he obtained through fraudulent prescriptions. Edmund had discovered the fraud and planned to report it to the medical board. The gate log proves Marsh arrived at 8:55 PM, not 9:35 PM as he claimed, which gave him time to slip the drug into the brandy tray left unattended in the hallway. Clara has a continuous video alibi, Victor left the estate before Marsh arrived, and Mrs. Pritchard poured the brandy from a sealed bottle in front of the cook.
